text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P0 pager - multi-GPU NCCL errors detected on tp4 cluster (tensor/pipeline parallel jobs). Auto-alert triggered for repeated NCCL timeouts and CUDA Xid errors across multiple nodes. Root nodes: gpu-045, gpu-046, gpu-051. Impacting in-flight training jobs.
oncall-bot: Summary: NCCL timeouts + Xid 79/13 observed, intermittent collectives hang, ~37% of TP jobs seeing stall or fail over last 40m.
alex-h: I'm oncall for infra, looking now. grabbing logs from gpu-045.
sam-r: I'll pull runtime metrics and recent image roll history. Any deploys in last 2 hours?
maya-ml: Affected job is TP4 w/ seq_len=8192 and large KV cache. Could be memory fragmentation + driver mismatch.
julie-sre: Steps: isolate nodes, cordon/drain if needed, capture nvml and dmesg, then try restarting container runtime. Keep customers looped.
alex-h: Got initial logs. attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] NCCL ERROR Fatal: NCCL COMM 0x7f8e2a - timeout in allreduce
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] CUDA Error: Xid 79 - GPU page fault or illegal memory access
[2026-03-15T14:02:14Z] pmap: OOM killer invoked for pid 8421
```

sam-r: Thanks. No control-plane deploys in last 3h. But there was a runtime image push for cudnn/driver variants 525.85 -> 525.90 on gpu-pool last night. Rolling back candidate.
ops_lead: If nodal cordon doesn't stop customer impact, prepare fallback routing to dedicated-region-1 where we run quantized replicas. Sam, can you patch routing?
sam-r: On it. Creating temporary routing policy to send new TP4 jobs to `dedicated-tp-quant`. Also lowering default batch size via FF to reduce per-GPU memory pressure.
maya-ml: Suggest enabling `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` on affected job group. Also set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` to reduce fragmentation.
alex-h: Applying env changes to affected deployment group now and restarting pods one at a time to preserve rendezvous order. Running: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-045
kubectl drain gpu-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
kubectl rollout restart ds/tp-runtime -n tp-jobs --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-046
```

julie-sre: Cordon succeeded for gpu-045. Drain in progress. Notifying support.
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by alex-h. Escalation to infra lead in 5m if not stabilized.

alex-h: Drain finished but one pod failed to evacuate due to a stuck NCCL communicator. For that pod we did a forced delete to let the scheduler recreate on gpu-051.
sam-r: I see driver mismatches on gpu-046 during log correlation - modules show mixed CUDA runtime versions on host. Rolling host driver upgrade rollback now.
maya-ml: We observed repeated `ncclCommDestroy` stack traces and `collective timeout` at step boundaries — looks like communicator tear-down race. Reducing parallelism and forcing smaller micro-batches reduced error rate from 37% -> 8% on test replica.
julie-sre: Customer impact note: Two enterprise customers had active TP training jobs. Customer A experienced partial step loss and retries; Customer B had one job terminate early (job id j-8921). CS notified and preparing postmortem communication.
ops_lead: Good. Also capture kernel logs and lspci for gpu firmware; request hardware triage if host driver rollback doesn't fix.
sam-r: Routing change applied. New job creations now go to `dedicated-tp-quant`. Existing in-flight jobs on affected nodes either restarted or evicted.
alex-h: Running healthchecks: 3/3 pods recreated OK on gpu-051, metrics stable for 2m. Continuing to monitor NCCL error count.
julie-sre: Marking incident P0 -> active mitigation. ETA for full recovery depends on hardware rollbacks and validation.
pagerduty: Reminder: next on-call handoff in 30m. Schedule handoff if extended.

alex-h: Leaving a short runbook in thread:
- cordon/drain affected nodes (gpu-045/gpu-046)
- set env: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
- reduce TP parallelism / micro-batch size flag flip
- route new jobs to dedicated-tp-quant fallback
- capture dmesg, nvml, lspci, driver versions, and collect kube events
- escalate to hardware if driver rollback fails

jane-sre: Taking over monitoring for next shift. I have notes and runbook; will continue escalation with infra if we see >5% error regression.

alex-h: handing off to jane-sre at 1752468400. I will remain available for 15m for context. Good work team. :thumbsup:
